newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures rise as yen slips.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures rise as yen slips.

text.p: Most Tokyo precious metal futures extended early gains to settle higher on Tuesday in lacklustre trade, as the dollar posted modest gains against the yen later in the day, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 11 yen to 15 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark December was up 14 yen at 1,348 yen.
In the morning session, profit-taking by individual investors put a lid on prices, but trade house buying of gold futures gathered force later in line with the currency market.
Spot gold was quoted at $345.65/346.05 per ounce at 0735 GMT, against $346.40/90 in New York on Monday.
One trader said spot gold prices were likely to consolidate at around the current levels.

A focus point for gold is the meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday of the U.S. Fed's policy-making committee, with a watch for U.S. stock market reaction, although market participants expect interest rates to be left unchanged.
Platinum futures posted dobule-digit gains, while most palladium futures hit their life-of-contract highs.
Traders said speculation that Russian platinum stocks are approaching a floor provided psychological support to platinum prices.
Although Russian palladium supplies were believed to be ample, the delayed export talks are likely to help palladium prices edge up further, traders said.
Platinum futures ranged from 10 yen to 14 yen per gram higher, with most-active benchmark December ending up 14 yen at 1,367 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from three to 10 yen per gram firmer. Most-active benchmark December was up three at 486.
Benchmark December silver was up 2.1 yen per 10 grams at 193.5 yen.
